Stated Claim / Post Context:
Missouri teacher who started OnlyFans account to pay the bills loses job

Sheen Sittner said she was recently let go from her teaching role after a Missouri school district discovered her OnlyFans account.

Actual Article Body:
By EMMA RICHTER, US SENIOR NEWS REPORTER

Published:  00:31 AEST, 27 September 2026   |  Updated:  03:57 AEST, 28 September 2026

387

View  comments

A Missouri substitute teacher who started an OnlyFans account to make extra cash lost her job after her employer discovered her profile, she said.

Sheena Sittner, 42, said she was recently let go from her role after Kelly Services, an outside contractor, was made aware of her online page.

Kelly Services had assigned Sittner to work at Parkway elementary school last year, a district spokesperson with Parkway Schools told the Daily Mail. She was not employed by the district.

The mother hit out at the education system, suggesting that if teachers made more money, then maybe she wouldn't have had to look for money elsewhere.

'If teachers were paid better, women wouldn’t have to resort to online content creation,' Sittner told KTVI. 'Sex sells.'

Sittner, of Ballwin, said she was a substitute teacher at her child's school and that she had been in that role as long as she's been an adult online content creator.

'It’s funny because I’ve had this account, this OnlyFans account, for two-plus years,' the mother told the outlet.

'So, whoever did find it did some deep-dive digging, because two years later and now it’s being found out.'

Sheena Sittner, 42, said she was recently let go from her role at Parkway Schools after her OnlyFans page was discovered

She said she had been working as a substitute teacher for Parkway Schools as long as her online account has been active. (Pictured: Administrative building for Parkway Schools)

She also admitted that she knew that one day her online presence would be uncovered, 'because whatever you put online, it’s on there forever.'

Sittner added: 'I didn’t, however, think that I would be completely stripped away from being at my kid’s school.'

Kelly Education had sent her an email that said she is suspended, pending termination, she told the outlet.

The email also read: 'Please refrain from contacting any school or districts,' she shared.

Sittner was left furious by this message because she said she can no longer volunteer at her child's school.

'It’s like all of a sudden I’ve done something so wrong and sinful that I’m not even allowed to volunteer at his school.

'I can find another job. I can handle the backlash and the criticism, but when it affects my child or my children, that’s where I draw the line,' she explained.

Despite her claim about volunteering, Kelly Education said that is not the case.

'It does not, and cannot, limit anyone’s right as a parent. Nothing in our request restricts their participation in their child’s education,' the agency told the outlet.

A spokesperson with Parkway Schools echoed that statement to the Daily Mail, stating that Sittner remains 'an active volunteer in our schools.'

All volunteers must complete a background check and mandatory training. Sittner has met those requirements, the district said.

She hit out at the education system, suggesting that if teachers were paid more, maybe she wouldn't have had to look for money elsewhere

Meanwhile, Sittner said her online profile will not interfere with her professional career.

'My personal life is completely separate from my professional life. I have kept those two separate forever.'

According to her Facebook profile, Sittner stopped working for Parkway Schools on September 8. She also had her OnlyFans link in her bio, but it is unclear when she added it.

The Daily Mail contacted Sittner, Parkway Schools and Kelly Education for comment.
